paper_title: Competitive ratio vs regret minimization: achieving the best of both worlds

For instance, in the paging problem, where the cache has k out of n pages, the number of states is N = Ω(nk ). However, we can show how to run our online algorithm in time polynomial in n and k. Adaptivity has attained much attention in the online learning literature over the years (an incomplete list includes Herbster and Warmuth (1998); Bousquet and Warmuth (2003); Blum and Mansour (2007); Hazan and Seshadhri (2007); Kapralov and Panigrahy (2011); Cesa- Bianchi et al. (2012); Adamskiy et al. (2012); Panigrahy and Popat (2013); Luo and Schapire (2015); Daniely et al. (2015); Altschuler and Talwar (2018). Another related, but somewhat orthogonal line of work Zinkevich (2003); Hall and Willett (2013); Rakhlin and Sridharan (2013); Jadbabaie et al. (2015) studies drifting environments. Switching costs were studied in Kalai and Vempala (2005) and attained considerable interest recently (e.g, Geulen et al. (2010); Cesa-Bianchi et al. (2013); Dekel et al. (2014)). Connections between regret-minimization and competitiveness has been previously studied. In particular Blum et al. (2002); Blum and Burch (2000); Abernethy et al. (2010); Buchbinder et al. (2012) focus on algorithmic techniques that simultaneously apply to MTS and experts, and also show regret minimization algorithms for MTS an other online problems. Another example is Andrew et al. (2013) that studies tradeoffs between regret minimization and competitiveness for a certain online convex problem. Technically, the work of Kapralov and Panigrahy (2011) is quite close to our work. They showed an algorithm for the two experts √ problem that has essentially no regret w.r.t. one of the experts, and nearly optimal regret (Õ( T )) w.r.t. the second expert. They also showed that this result implies an algorithm with strongly adaptive guarantees in the N -experts problem. Namely, they showed an algorithm with nearly optimal regret on every geometric time interval. Our main contribution, regarding regret minimization, is to handle switching costs. In addition, we extend the regret bound to hold on all intervals.
